title: Module 4: Transaction Log & Replay
content: Mastering message durability and historical playback in AMPS. 🔄
Building resilient, resumable, and auditable applications.

title: What is the Transaction Log?
content: A sequential, historical record of all published messages. 📖
Stored in durable **Journal Files** on disk.
Ensures **persistence** and **consistency** across restarts.
Fully queryable through the AMPS Client API (unlike standard DB logs).
The foundation for HA, Replication, and Message Queues.

title: How it Works: The Journaling Flow
content: Messages are appended sequentially to the active journal file.
mermaid:
graph LR
    P[Publisher] -->|Message + Seq#| A[AMPS Server]
    A -->|Append| J[Active Journal File]
    J -->|Rotate if Full| J2[New Journal File]
    A -->|Ack| P
    A -.->|Replay| S[Subscriber]

title: Core Concepts: Journal Files
content: **Sequential Files**: AMPS writes to multiple files (journals) of fixed size. 📑
**Immutable**: Once a message is written, it is never modified.
**Configurable Retention**: Auto-archive or delete based on age or size.
**Sequential I/O**: Optimized for the maximum throughput of your storage device.

title: Bookmarks: The Universal Pointer
content: Every message in the log has a unique **Bookmark**. 🔖
Composed of: `Publisher ID` + `Sequence Number`.
**Monotonically Increasing**: Allows AMPS to find points in time instantly.
Bookmarks are consistent across a replicated network of AMPS instances.

title: Configuring the Transaction Log
content: Enable logging in the `TransactionLog` section of `config.xml`.

title: Bookmark Subscriptions
content: A subscription that starts from a specific bookmark. 🎯
**EPOCH**: Start from the beginning of the log (replays everything).
**NOW**: Start from the live stream (no historical replay).
**Timestamp**: Start from a specific date/time.
**Specific Bookmark**: Resume exactly where you left off.

title: Replay Flow: History to Live
content: AMPS replays history, then seamlessly cuts over to live messages.
mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Subscriber
    participant A as AMPS Server
    participant J as Journal
    S->>A: Subscribe(Bookmark=EPOCH)
    loop Replay Phase
        A->>J: Read historical messages
        J-->>A: Message Data
        A-->>S: Deliver replayed message
    end
    Note over A,S: Cutover to Live
    rect rgb(200, 255, 200)
        A-->>S: Deliver new live publish
    end

title: Advanced Replay: Rate Control
content: Don't let history overwhelm your client! 🏎️
**Absolute Rate**: `rate=1000` (messages/sec).
**Bandwidth Rate**: `rate=500KB` (bytes/sec).
**Multiplier**: `rate=2X` (replay twice as fast as originally published).
**Gap Control**: `rate_max_gap=10s` (skip over quiet periods).

title: Replay Windows: Start & Stop
content: Request a specific slice of history using `[start:end)`. 🪟
**Inclusive `[` / `]`**: Include the boundary bookmark.
**Exclusive `(` / `)`**: Skip the boundary bookmark.
Useful for auditing specific events or bulk processing historical data.

title: Pause and Resume
content: Control the flow of a bookmark subscription. ⏸️
**Pause**: AMPS stops sending but keeps your position in the log.
**Resume**: AMPS starts back up exactly where it paused.
Synchronize multiple subscriptions to replay at the same pace.
Note: Pausing a live subscription is generally not recommended (pacing is better handled by rate control).

title: High Availability (HA) Integration
content: The Transaction Log is the backbone of HA. 🏗️
**Reliable Publishing**: Ack sent only after message is safely on disk.
**Resumable Subscriptions**: Clients use bookmarks to ensure 'exactly-once' processing.
**Replication Catch-up**: Standby servers replay logs from the primary to synchronize.

title: Best Practices
content: Use **fast storage** (SSD/NVMe) for journals. 🚀
Separate the journal directory from the OS/Application drive.
Implement a **Retention Policy** (archiving/deletion) to manage disk space.
Always use **unique client names** for resumable subscriptions.
Monitor journal disk usage and write latencies.

title: Summary
content: Transaction Log = Durable, Sequential History. ✅
Bookmarks = Pointers to specific messages. ✅
Bookmark Subscriptions = Flexible Replay & Recovery. ✅
Essential for production-grade, highly available systems. ✅
